title: Escalation Rollup Wizard and Cost Fallback Visualizer
creator: Ava Patel
description: Prototype a guided 'Escalation Rollup Wizard' in the Redwood Console that helps teams compose multi-tier alert policies with explicit escalation sequencing, SLA tension indicators, and an integrated 'Cost Fallback Visualizer' that simulates fallback routing to lower-cost model variants or regions. The flow should produce compact alert configs that auto-populate postmortem links and on-call transfer microcopy for smoother incident transitions. Deliverables: Figma prototype, copy deck, interaction spec, and a short usability report from initial sessions.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard screens map to 3 core steps: Targets (who/where), Escalation (who after how long), Fallbacks & Cost (routing and cost estimate)
Inline SLO tension bar shows projected SLO delta for each escalation policy and flags any high-risk combos
Cost Fallback Visualizer shows estimated per-hour cost delta and expected latency change for each routing choice
Generated alert object includes fields for 'postmortem_link' and 'handoff_snippet' that are editable before save
Prototype reviewed by PM and runtime eng and a usability session with 3 on-call engineers recorded with at least 3 actionable findings
design_notes: Primary goal: reduce cognitive load when creating multi-tier alerts for services with mixed Dedicated/Hosted deployments
Use progressive disclosure: only surface advanced routing and quantization fallbacks after basic escalation is set
SLO tension computation will be an approximate projection (front-end model) and annotated as 'estimation' to avoid false precision
Cost estimates are guided by current catalog pricing and per-model throughput profiles; UX should call out assumptions and link to the cost model page
decisions: Show three escalation tiers by default (Primary, Secondary, Auto-fallback) with ability to add more
Collapse low-frequency routing options under 'Advanced redirect' to keep primary flow lean
Make postmortem_link optional but surfaced in the final review step with a recommended template
Use a small inline sparkline to communicate historical alerting frequency in the Targets step
tradeoffs: Surface more guidance vs speed: added help copy increases time to complete but reduces misconfigurations
Accurate cost projections vs privacy: we avoid querying billing at design time and use conservative estimates instead
Client-side SLO projection (fast) vs server-side canonical calculation (accurate). We will label projections as estimates and re-run server-side validations on save
